correctness.summary: Run is an unimplemented stub: it only initializes matchLeft[]/matchRight[] to -1 and computes no assignment. For any cost matrix it returns an empty matching, which is wrong whenever an assignment of positive size exists.
correctness.triggeringInput: cost (n*m row-major) = {1,2, 2,1}, n=2, m=2, matchLeft=stackalloc int[2], matchRight=stackalloc int[2]. Expected optimal assignment matchLeft[0]=0, matchLeft[1]=1; actual leaves all entries -1.
correctness.rootCause: The rectangular Hungarian algorithm body is missing; only the -1 initialization loops are present.
correctness.suggestedFix: Implement the O(n^2 m) Hungarian (Jonker-Volgenant style) on the n x m cost matrix, padding to square or handling the rectangular case, and write the resulting assignment into matchLeft/matchRight.

perf.summary: Stub: only initializes matchLeft/matchRight to -1; the Hungarian rectangular algorithm body is unimplemented.
perf.currentCost: Two O(n)/O(m) init loops and no solving work; cost parameter unused.
perf.proposedChange: Implement the Jonker-Volgenant / Hungarian core, or document as init-only. The two init loops are over different lengths (n vs m) and cannot be fused unless min/max handled; leave as-is.
perf.rationale: Primary signal is the missing algorithm; no micro-opt available on a pure two-loop initializer beyond what Burst already does.
perf.risk: Implementing changes observable outputs by design; nothing to optimize in the current no-op safely.
